purpose: Exploratory material-physics report, not a final convergence/submission claim
claim: Similar net electrical gains in MoSSe and InSe conceal very different layer-resolved changes: InSe has large opposing increments, while MoSSe is predominantly changed on its upper layer.
question: Does interface mixing link the rewritten layer response to electrical control in a different orbital system?
archetype: Measured-control comparison plus a Hamiltonian intervention

panels.a: Net gate-induced change: screened bilayer, isolated pair, specified electrostatic reference
panels.b: Signed lower/upper changes under the same actual gate, compared with a matched isolated layer
panels.c: Signed layer contributions to net gain, normalized by the matched isolated-pair gate slope: isolated reference, MoSSe, InSe. Net shown as their sum.

statistics: Deterministic calculations, not samples. No statistical errors/p-values. Alternate cutoffs/windows shown as sensitivity, never confidence intervals.
scope: Fixed geometry, neutral insulating Ex Bz Pauli-spin response. Gate-SCF; subsequent probe and mixing controls use frozen screened potentials. This figure compares actual gate-SCF data and specified electrostatic reference; channel-intervention details remain in the accompanying results table.
fonts: Arial; labels 8pt, ticks >=7pt; editable vector text
final_qa: source validator plus local visual inspection; denser zero-gate check must be reported separately
